- `9c53a0de2e7964bf` [general] 'Are LLMs Ready for TOON?' (arXiv:2601.12014): the format-without-native-support cost is capacity-dependent. TOON cuts tokens −26.4% vs JSON, −49.4% vs XML, −15.3% vs YAML and estimated carbon −82.9%/−87.6%/−76.9%, but structural correctness collapses — GCS 0.513 vs JSON 0.840, YAML 0.872, XML 0.563 — because TOON is enforced only via prompts. Llama 3.3 70B shows no statistically significant difference (p>0.05 vs all formats), while Gemma 3 4B fails nearly completely (TOON GCS 0.045 vs JSON 0.779) and Qwen 3 4B drops 0.769→0.334. Novel formats are only usable on models with enough capacity to internalize unseen structural constraints.

- `0a6c3cc372c5cf77` [repair] Enforcement cost is implementation-determined (measured): with mask-cache + CPU/GPU overlap, XGrammar mask generation drops to <40 µs/token ('up to 100×' vs regex/CFG baselines, ~zero end-to-end overhead), though the fastest configuration can be the most permissive (XGrammar's highest under-constraint count on the JSON Schema Test Suite); parser-stack classification gives O(1) vocabulary-independent masks (PSC, 700×/30× mask speedups, e2e throughput ≈ unconstrained); vLLM JSON-grammar constrained decoding: 3.6–8.2× inference latency with Gemma 52.4% duplicate outputs.

- `a5b5c576f4ffd0b5` [general] OpenAI's Structured Outputs launch post (2024-08-06, first-party vendor eval, not independently replicated): prompting alone <40% (gpt-4-0613), trained-only model 93% (gpt-4o-2024-08-06), 100% with strict constrained decoding. Guarantee holds only for a supported JSON-Schema subset, and 'Structured Outputs doesn't prevent all kinds of model mistakes'. One-time first-request cost: '<10 seconds... more complex schemas may take up to a minute' then cached. Shape is consistent with JSONSchemaBench's finding that closed-provider compliance is ~100% within their supported subset.

- `a668572194f1c30e` [general] The TMLR survey 'A Survey of Agent Memory in the Second Half' reports hundreds of agent-memory papers in 2025 and frames memory as the substrate of self-evolution: short-term memory gates which experiences are abstracted, long-term memory consolidates them into reusable knowledge and skills, and memory management itself is becoming a trainable capability. Source: arXiv 2602.06052.

- `dc228d975c9158da` [general] OpenAI Agents SDK guardrails are model-as-judge: input guardrails run before the main model, output guardrails validate final output, tool guardrails check arguments/results, and a tripwire blocks the run. Boundary caveat: input guardrails run only for the first agent in a chain and output guardrails only at the final-output agent, so checks belong next to the side-effecting tool in manager-style workflows.

- `0f170eb63104f9a4` [general] OpenAI Agents SDK hooks: `RunHooks`/`AgentHooks` receive `on_tool_start`/`on_tool_end` (immediately before/after a local tool is invoked) plus `on_agent_start/end`, `on_handoff`, `on_llm_start/end`, attached per-run or per-agent; the `@tool` wrapper adds the runtime pipeline (schema validation, context injection, guardrails, timeouts, failure handling, tracing) around the raw callable, and calling `__wrapped__` bypasses it.

- `293c648eb7e6dfe0` [repair] Intrinsic self-correction (measured, repair): without an external signal consistently lowers accuracy — GSM8K Llama-2 62.0→36.5, GPT-4 95.5→89.0 (1→5 calls, up to −25 pts) while multiplying call cost 1→5×; repair only reliably helps with external feedback — oracle labels, execution/unit-test signals (Self-Debugging +2–9% to +12%), or stronger/human feedback (1.58× more repaired programs pass, 33.3%→52.6%); at equal budget repair often ties or loses to plain i.i.d. resampling.

- `7b02843dca2475f6` [general] OpenAI Agents SDK built-in session backends: SQLiteSession is the default for 'local development and simple apps'; documented shared/multi-process paths are RedisSession ('shared memory across workers… low-latency distributed deployments'), SQLAlchemySession (Postgres etc.), MongoDBSession ('horizontally-scalable, multi-process session storage'), and DaprSession. Operational guidance: in-memory SQLite for temporary, file-based SQLite for persistent, Redis for shared low-latency, MongoDB for multi-process horizontally-scalable storage.

- `6977145a51d83491` [general] Hybrid LLM routing value depends sharply on the model-pair quality gap: at a 20% cost advantage the small-gap pair (Llama-2 7b/13b) loses <=0.1% BART quality, the large-gap pair (FLAN-t5 800m/Llama-2 13b) loses up to 5.8%. When the gap is large, training on Pr[H>=0] labels is near-useless ('0 for almost 90% of queries'); a label-relaxation transformation (Pr[H>=−t]) recovers a usable signal. (Hybrid LLM, arXiv 2404.14618v1, Table 1, §3.3, Fig 4a)

- `c65a4ce6cdb624b8` [general] Long-term cross-thread agent memory has a different shape than run state and is DB- or vector-store-backed in the frameworks. LangGraph's long-term memory is a Store abstraction (namespace + key + JSON value) with production backends PostgresStore, MongoDBStore, RedisStore, UpstashStore and optional semantic/vector search; the reference SQL schema uses TEXT[] namespace + JSONB value + GIN index.

- `104c7db4c0a0fa2a` [general] JSONSchemaBench (Geng et al., arXiv:2501.10868) measured empirical schema coverage on ~10K real-world schemas with Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct (greedy, 2-shot): LM-only compliance 0.90 (GlaiveAI), 0.65 (GitHub-Easy), 0.56 (Kubernetes), 0.46 (Snowplow), 0.38 (GitHub-Medium), 0.13 (GitHub-Hard), 0.21 (JSONSchemaStore). Prompting-only compliance collapses to 13–46% on medium-to-hard schemas; these are lower bounds for weak models, not frontier models.

- `1052dd5a927ed18a` [general] LoCoMo has three tasks: (1) QA in five categories — single-hop, multi-hop, temporal reasoning, open-domain (commonsense/world) knowledge, and adversarial (designed to trick the agent into providing wrong answers, with expectation the agent identifies them as unanswerable); (2) event-graph summarization scored with FactScore against the ground-truth temporal event graph; (3) multi-modal dialogue generation scored with MMRelevance.

- `07bdd35766db54d4` [repair] Enforcement guarantee is approximate (measured): the standard locally-constrained stack (Outlines/XGrammar/OpenAI) is distribution-biased (renormalizing over locally-valid tokens distorts sampling from p(x|constraint)) and can fail validity within a finite token budget — LCD constraint satisfaction 95.26–99.20% at fixed budgets vs 100% for budget-aware GCD (GCD ~1.1× latency; P-GCD probabilistic look-ahead 3.11–10.2×); on MoE architectures Outlines/LLGuidance/XGrammar give ~0 gain and Mixtral LLGuidance AST collapses 0.409→0.236; grammar scarcity is removable — learned CFGs from execution logs reach 0.91–1.00 precision vs 0.025 for formal induction (Autogrammar).

- `e232f1c2ce57f2cf` [general] MCP enforced contract: `inputSchema` MUST be a valid JSON Schema object (2020-12 default); `outputSchema` is optional but binding when present (servers MUST provide conforming structured results, clients SHOULD validate); tool annotations from non-trusted servers MUST be considered untrusted; servers MUST validate all inputs, enforce access controls, rate-limit, and sanitize outputs; clients SHOULD validate tool results before handing them to the LLM; there SHOULD be a human able to deny invocations; SEP-1303 routes input-validation failures into the `isError: true` tool-result channel.

- `74a333f06b0e1b1b` [general] Recurring across independent LLM-routing papers: (1) the achievable tradeoff is dominated by the size of the weak/strong quality gap and the training-data distribution match (augmentation and low-data regimes matter more than router architecture); (2) routers over-deploy the strong model in practice (RouterArena normalized deferral curve), so the frontier is far from the oracle; (3) router overhead itself is measurable and non-trivial (latency, embedding API calls, per-request cost) but small vs generation cost.

- `c1a0b768075c2467` [general] Verdict of the research: besides MAST there is a substantial, actively growing body of empirically derived LLM-agent failure taxonomies, all reporting explicit measurement corpora (trace counts, annotator counts, agreement statistics, task/turn counts); the strongest-documented are the Interaction-Centric Taxonomy (41 modes; 40 grounded worked examples; judge reproducibility kappa=0.76), DEFT (14 modes; grounded theory over ~1,000 DRA reports with Krippendorff's-alpha validation), Aegis (6 modes; 142 annotated failed traces), DeepVerifier (5 classes/13 sub-classes; 555 annotated error points), and the longitudinal silent-failure taxonomy (5 classes; 22 production incidents).

- `1150dfe53f759651` [general] 'Is Self-Repair a Silver Bullet for Code Generation?' (Olausson et al., ICLR 2024, arXiv:2306.09896): cost-aware repair gains are modest at equal budget and sometimes negative — GPT-3.5 on HumanEval ≤ +3%, Code Llama on HumanEval ≤ +10%, GPT-4 on APPS ≤ +8% over i.i.d. sampling at the same sample budget. Sample-budget allocation matters: on APPS, GPT-4 with 10 diverse initial samples + 1 repair each = 1.05x pass@20, but 2 initial + 10 repairs each = 0.97x vs pass@22 — over-investing in repair loses to plain resampling. Repair is bottlenecked by feedback quality: human feedback vs GPT-4's own raised repaired-program pass rate from 33.3% to 52.6% (1.58x); GPT-4 feedback judged inaccurate in 32/80 cases vs 7/80 for humans.

- `49e58f71d2bdd715` [evidence-status] Anthropic Claude Code documents enforcement tiers for checks: in-prompt iteration; `/goal` condition re-checked by a separate evaluator every turn; a Stop hook that runs the check as a script and blocks the turn from ending until it passes (overridden after 8 consecutive blocks); and a verification subagent where a fresh model tries to refute the result so the worker isn't grading itself.

- `53b44257c13294e1` [general] Hybrid LLM routes each query to exactly one of two models (large vs small), never calling multiple LLMs per query. The router is a BERT-style encoder (DeBERTa-v3-large) trained to predict the quality gap H(x)=q(S(x))−q(L(x)) where q is BART score; a test-time threshold on the router score trades quality for cost. (Hybrid LLM, arXiv 2404.14618v1, §2.2, §3.1-3.3)

- `b25f3d9404e1c402` [repair] Error-budget masking mechanism (Jang et al.): the score stays flat because the benchmark allows ten failed tool calls per episode and per-error recovery is equally reliable at both precisions (55% recovery rate unchanged) — 'the loop actively repairs the errors quantization introduces before they reach the outcome' at the cost of 2.5× more failed calls per episode (1.45→3.64) and 29% more tool calls (7.3→9.4); falsifiable proof: shrinking the error budget K re-exposes the damage — the BF16−INT4 gap grows 1.3 pp (K=10) to 7.5 (K=5) to 16.7 pp (K=2), ~13× wider, only in the volume-adding cell; budget-exhausting terminations rise 9× (5→46 of 456); mechanism: logit-margin account — full-precision failure propensity gates susceptibility (near-zero-baseline Qwen cells not amplified; checkpoint identity, not size/architecture, decides).

- `6e30b9e0905d102a` [general] Established multi-source finding: showing a calibrated confidence score helps operators when the score is the operative mechanism — it improved trust calibration (Zhang 2020), machine and human confidence each significantly improved hybrid human+AI accuracy within a narrow accuracy band (Steyvers 2022), and uncertainty-based abstention improved deployed clinical accuracy ~20-25 points (Wienholt 2026).

- `6e1f98afd067dae7` [repair] Palabrita resolution architecture (reported): defensive parsing as a pipeline (UTF-8 sanitize → code-fence strip → direct decode → regex extract → structural type-based field inference), contextual retry feeding the specific rejection reason back into the prompt (word-length errors the main trigger), and 'progressive simplification' — the LLM's job reduced from 7 output fields to 0 for word generation (curated word lists) and 2 fields for hints, with a deterministic fallback so 'the LLM enhances the experience; it does not gate it'.

- `a6e2c69032154967` [general] LoCoMo findings: long-context LLMs/RAG improve QA 22–66% but significantly lag human levels (by 56%), especially in temporal reasoning (by 73%); long-context models are especially prone to misassigning dialogs or events to the wrong speaker; gpt-3.5-turbo-16k scored 2.1% on adversarial questions. - `9cc229d3928af9fd` [general] RouteLLM trains a binary 'win prediction' router P_θ(wins|q) from Chatbot Arena human preference data and routes to the strong model iff P(wins|q) >= cost threshold α. Four parameterizations: similarity-weighted (SW) Bradley–Terry ranking, matrix factorization, BERT classifier, causal LLM classifier (Llama 3 8B). (RouteLLM, arXiv 2406.18665v4, §3.1, §4.2)

- `68944cdb3db0a2fc` [general] Retrieval techniques are complements, not alternatives — the biggest gains come from stacking them: Zep = temporal KG + hybrid lexical/dense/graph retrieval; HippoRAG = KG + embeddings + PPR; LongMemEval's best config = session decomposition + fact-augmented keys + time-aware query expansion. Sources: arXiv:2501.13956; arXiv:2405.14831; arXiv:2410.10813v2.

- `9d1f310048daf8ef` [repair] Melo (system report) is the retry-economics anchor the literature otherwise lacks: retry loop's true cost is latency arithmetic (a rare +4.1 s amortized / +15.9 s triggered measured pair), its benefit is converting otherwise-empty sessions into usable ones, and its failure mode is silent constraint degradation (23% of recoveries) — a production retry must be evaluated on recovery AND preservation, not recovery alone.

- `e5170e596b2575e1` [repair] SQL Query Engine (system report) validates retry-loop design with three explicit mechanisms: early-accept (never re-evaluate a query that executed correctly — prevents the LLM 'fixing' a good query into a bad one), best-result tracking (return the best result seen when retries exhaust — a bad retry cannot regress), and ignoring the LLM's own isValid self-assessment (always False by design; only execution outcome determines success).

- `0bcb6001a27bbb57` [ai-auditability] AI RMF Playbook Govern: GOVERN 1.1 'Legal and regulatory requirements involving AI are understood, managed, and documented'; GOVERN 1.4 urges standardized documentation (AI-actor contact info, business justification, scope and usages, expected risks, assumptions and limitations, training-data characterization, algorithmic methodology, testing and validation results, dependencies, deployment/monitoring/change-management plans) plus a 'model documentation inventory'; GOVERN 1.5 covers ongoing monitoring, incident response, and 'appeal and override' (human adjudication of system outcomes); GOVERN 2.1 requires roles, responsibilities, and lines of communication to be 'documented and clear.'

- `8eff920971cc7319` [general] Claude Code hooks fire per session (`SessionStart`/`SessionEnd`), per turn (`UserPromptSubmit`, `Stop`), and on every tool call (`PreToolUse`, `PostToolUse`, `PostToolUseFailure`, plus `PermissionRequest`/`PermissionDenied`); handlers can be shell commands, HTTP endpoints, MCP tools, LLM prompts, or subagents; `matcher` (tool name/regex) + `if` (permission-rule syntax) filter them; MCP tools match as `mcp__<server>__<tool>`; hooks can return `permissionDecision: 'deny'` to block a call; hooks live in settings files, managed policy, plugin `hooks/hooks.json`, or skill/agent frontmatter; `allowManagedHooksOnly` lets enterprises suppress user/project/plugin hooks.

- `32bed97e81d99774` [evidence-status] SWE-bench counts `resolved` only when the post-patch repo passes the required tests, so the oracle can disagree with a solved-looking patch. The quantitative wrong-but-passing-patch numbers (~28.5% of a SWE-bench sample passes a Docker-verified incorrect patch; 7.8% of counted-correct patches fail the developer suite; one-in-five 'solved' patches semantically wrong) are estimates reported only in mini-agi's research doc citing preprints (2606.16062, 2503.15223, 2603.00520) that were not fetched — unconfirmed, flagged preprint; treat as calibration targets only after replication.

- `d1b3d3ef01bfcfff` [ai-auditability] Opinion: the weakness of a bare decision log is integrity and non-repudiation — OWASP states plain logs cannot reliably provide it without signatures; the evidence-chain standards supply exactly the missing machinery (signed Statements bound to subjects by digest, provenance predicates, proof chains). The suggested shape is a decision log whose entries embed digest references bound by an attestation/evidence chain, with approval records as human-signed gates on top — not one mechanism chosen over the others.

- `6665ad2250b0bf6a` [general] The three approaches (WAL+checkpoint, snapshot-restore, event sourcing) are one family, not alternatives: every credible system (PostgreSQL, SQLite, WiredTiger/MongoDB, RocksDB, etcd/Raft, Temporal, LangGraph, AWS Step Functions) combines an append-only, checksummed, order-preserving log with periodic state snapshots that bound replay.

- `ede50378a375dcb5` [evidence-status] Terminal-Bench/Harbor: each task is an instruction + a test script + an oracle solution; the Harbor format requires `tests/test.sh` to write a reward to `/logs/verifier/reward.txt` (e.g. `1`/`0`) or `reward.json`, with a canonical pytest-exit-code -> reward mapping. Beyond that, policy for logical behavior and information flow should be managed with... potentially, an LSM of your choosing.' Direct corollary: seccomp alone is insufficient as a worker sandbox; an LSM layer (Landlock is one) is the documented complement (opinion derived directly from that statement).

- `76649269e1ba035d` [general] Seccomp userspace notification (SECCOMP_RET_USER_NOTIF) reintroduces TOCTOU and is explicitly not a security mechanism: 'the seccomp user-space notification mechanism can not be used to implement a security policy'; SECCOMP_USER_NOTIF_FLAG_CONTINUE has a time-of-check/time-of-use race because the target can rewrite syscall arguments while blocked; a notifier 'can be bypassed if the existing filters allow the use of seccomp(2) or prctl(2) to install a filter' with higher-precedence action.

- `3880083953a8f0d3` [general] Gradle Test Retry plugin retries failed tests within the same task up to maxRetries (default 0 = off); defaults: failOnPassedAfterRetry=false (pass-on-retry does not fail the task), failOnSkippedAfterRetry=true, maxFailures=0 (circuit-breaker cap off). Supports include/exclude filters by class name and annotations, plus whole-class retry (classRetry) for Spock @Stepwise/TestNG dependsOn. The README warns retrying tests alone is not a viable flaky-test mitigation strategy and should accompany tracking/fixing.

- `0ad6075069f5864a` [general] Complementarity has narrow preconditions: a hybrid human+AI pair beats both human-only and machine-only ensembles only when the two classifiers perform within a bounded accuracy band, and the key limiting factor is the latent correlation between human and machine confidence (observed ~0.4 for human+AI vs ~0.7 human-human); effective AI advice should be accurate and statistically independent of human judgment. (Steyvers et al., PNAS 2022)

- `24f290b647ef095e` [general] Kubernetes quarantines a single test by adding [Flaky] to its test name; most CI jobs exclude these tests, which run only in explicitly flaky jobs (e.g. the gci-gce-flaky job). Quarantining a presubmit test requires a release-milestone issue labeled priority/critical-urgent, lifecycle/frozen, and kind/flake, with the owning SIG expected to fix and reintroduce or delete the test. Whole-suite quarantine uses [Feature:Foo] names plus dedicated jobs, which merge-blocking suites avoid unless proven non-flaky.
